title: The scoring fix, tested

tuning.note: Presets are re-tuned per priority on the validation split alone, with the frozen recipe's grids, accuracy floors and tie-breaks. The reliability grid replaces 0 with the floor 0.25, so it is (0.25, 0.5); the chosen reliability weights are cost 0.25, quality 0.5, latency 0.25, balanced 0.25. Cost and time use fixed references, here the training-split estimates' largest expected cost and time per task group. In an unchanged pool those equal the largest among the available models, so the fixed scoring differs from the frozen one only through the reliability weight and when a model's price, speed or availability changes.

protocol: The frozen router is data/learned/cp3-router-model.json, exported on 2026-11-03, and remains the evaluated system. Nothing in it, in final-evaluation.json or in any other committed report changes.

The fixed variant has the same classifier and features. It divides each model's expected cost and time by fixed references, the largest expected cost and time per task group among the frozen pool's estimates, instead of the largest among the available models, and gives reliability a small default weight.

The reliability weight and the presets were chosen on the Checkpoint 3 validation split only, with the frozen recipe: a classifier refit on the training split, the same weight grids, accuracy floors and tie-breaks, and the reliability grid floored at 0.25. The recipe rerun with the old normalization and grid reproduces the frozen presets.

The questions were fixed in code (FIXED_QUESTIONS) on 2026-11-26 before any result of the fixed variant was read. p-values are exact McNemar tests on the prompts where exactly one of two settings is right, Holm-adjusted together within each evaluation.

'Told' is the router that learns the change, as the live catalog or call monitoring would tell it; 'old estimates' keeps its trained estimates. Both use the same presets in the same changed world, and neither is retrained.
Everything is offline replay of the committed cell table (cells.jsonl); no provider is called.
caveats: The fresh prompts are read again here (they were used for the frozen evaluation, its robustness scenarios and the two pool studies). Nothing was tuned on them: the fixed variant's presets come from the validation split.
The fixed variant is a tested recommendation, not the evaluated system: the frozen router remains the one whose held-out results were reported.
The references are stored in this report, not in the router file, which stays byte-identical to the frozen export.

The scenarios were chosen after the flaws were found, so they are the cases the fix was built for. They show that the fix repairs those cases; they do not show it is better in situations nobody tested.
The Gemma 4 26B scenario replays the failed calls with Mercury 3's real 404 time, since no real calls to Gemma 4 26B after it went away were made.

questions.question: With no change, does the fixed scoring keep accuracy on the fresh prompts at each priority?
questions.rule: Yes if no priority has fewer right answers than the frozen router with a Holm-adjusted McNemar p below 0.05 (four priorities, one family with the scenario tests).
questions.answer_fresh: Fixed against frozen, right answers and change in spend: cost 264 against 265 (Holm p 1.000, spend +$0.0142); quality 282 against 282 (Holm p 1.000, spend +$0); latency 276 against 276 (Holm p 1.000, spend +$0); balanced 276 against 276 (Holm p 1.000, spend +$0).
questions.answer_test: Fixed against frozen, right answers and change in spend: cost 105 against 103 (Holm p 1.000, spend +$0.0084); quality 112 against 112 (Holm p 1.000, spend +$0); latency 104 against 102 (Holm p 1.000, spend +$0.0033); balanced 104 against 102 (Holm p 1.000, spend +$0.0033).

questions.question: In 'slowest three models 3x slower', does the fastest setting get faster (median time) when told, unlike the frozen router?
questions.rule: Yes if the fixed variant's median time when told is below its median time with old estimates.
questions.answer_fresh: Fixed scoring, told: 3.84 s median (276 right, $0.43) against 3.84 s with old estimates (276 right, $0.43); with nothing changed it takes 3.84 s. Frozen router, told: 7.11 s against 3.84 s.
questions.answer_test: Fixed scoring, told: 2.56 s median (104 right, $0.12) against 2.56 s with old estimates (104 right, $0.12); with nothing changed it takes 2.56 s. Frozen router, told: 3.17 s against 2.09 s.

questions.question: In 'most expensive model 4x pricier', does the lowest-cost setting stop shifting spend to other models, and does best quality reduce its use of that model?
questions.rule: Yes if, told rather than with old estimates, the lowest-cost setting sends at most 5 percentage points more prompts to Gemma 4 26B and spends at most twice as much, and best quality sends fewer prompts to Gemini 4 Argon.
questions.answer_fresh: Lowest cost, fixed scoring: 100 prompts to Gemma 4 26B when told against 100 with old estimates, spending $0.0176 against $0.0176 (frozen: 100 against 22, $0.0176 against $0.0034). Best quality, fixed scoring: 0 prompts to Gemini 4 Argon when told against 197 (frozen: 196 against 197), 265 right for $0.0243 against 282 for $3.84 (Holm p 0.00017): the best-quality setting reacts fully to the price, at a cost in right answers.
questions.answer_test: Lowest cost, fixed scoring: 40 prompts to Gemma 4 26B when told against 40 with old estimates, spending $0.0087 against $0.0087 (frozen: 40 against 2, $0.0087 against $0.0003). Best quality, fixed scoring: 0 prompts to Gemini 4 Argon when told against 79 (frozen: 78 against 79), 105 right for $0.0122 against 112 for $1.68 (Holm p 0.43): the best-quality setting reacts fully to the price, at a cost in right answers.

questions.question: In 'free remote models fail 50%', does the lowest-cost setting hold its accuracy when told, without a hand-raised weight?
questions.rule: Yes if, told, it keeps at least 95% of its right answers with nothing changed and gets more right than with old estimates.
questions.answer_fresh: Lowest cost, fixed scoring: 268 right when told, 172 with old estimates, 264 with no outage ($0.0309 told). Frozen router: 137 told, 137 old, 265 with no outage.
questions.answer_test: Lowest cost, fixed scoring: 103 right when told, 72 with old estimates, 105 with no outage ($0.0151 told). Frozen router: 48 told, 48 old, 103 with no outage.

scenario.title: No change
scenario.description: Nothing changes: the router as it would be deployed, as the reference for every other scenario.

scenario.title: Observed drift (Nov 12-13)
scenario.description: OpenRouter stopped serving Mercury 3 and cut Gemma 4 26B's price by 12%. The router that is told learns both from the live catalog; with its old estimates it still sends prompts to Mercury, and those calls fail.

scenario.title: Gemma 4 26B and Mercury 3 unavailable
scenario.description: On 2026-11-26 the live catalog check found Gemma 4 26B A4B no longer served by its pinned host (NextBit), after Mercury 3's retirement on 2026-11-12. The router that is told excludes both; with old estimates it still sends prompts to them, and those calls fail. Calls to a model that went away are replayed as failures after 0.4 s (Mercury's real 404 time). On the fresh prompts, the router with old estimates still has the 2026-11-13 catalog, so Mercury 3 is already excluded.

scenario.title: Gemma 4 26B costs 30x more
scenario.description: The cheap paid model becomes about as expensive as Gemini 4 Argon.

scenario.title: Gemini 4 Argon costs 4x more
scenario.description: The most expensive model gets dearer. Costs are scored relative to the most expensive model, so this tests whether the router still reacts.

scenario.title: Gemini 4 Argon costs a quarter
scenario.description: The strongest model gets much cheaper.

scenario.title: Free OVHcloud endpoints 3x slower
scenario.description: gpt-oss-120b, Llama 3.3 70B and Qwen 3.8 27B answer three times slower.

scenario.title: Gemma 4 26B 3x slower
scenario.description: The cheap paid model's host slows down threefold.

scenario.title: Free endpoints fail half the time
scenario.description: Half of all calls to the four free remote models fail after 2 s. The tuned settings give reliability no weight, so the router knows the new failure rate but does not avoid the failing models.

scenario.title: Same outage, reliability weighted
scenario.description: The same outage with the user's reliability weight raised from 0 to 1, so a known failure rate counts against a model.

scenario.title: Gemini 4 Argon fails 30% of calls
scenario.description: A partial outage of the strongest model, with reliability weighted at 1.

notes: Outcomes are the stored late-October calls; every scenario rescales them.
